company.name: Patlytics
company.source_note:
Patlytics is an AI-powered end-to-end patent platform — drafting, litigation, portfolio management. Saves attorneys up to 15 hours per patent application, $30,000 per claim chart. Clients include Rivian (converts raw data into attorney-editable drafts collaboratively), Xerox, Canon. 40%+ of AmLaw 100 firms use the platform. Series B launched autonomous AI agent roadmap for drafting, research, and portfolio triage.
~$65M total raised ($4.5M Seed + $14M Series A + $40M Series B) in <3 years; 40%+ of AmLaw 100 firms as clients
Founded 2024 (re-launched from earlier seed); 2010 founding origin for founders Paul Lee & Arthur Jen; corporate clients include Rivian, Xerox, Canon

outreach_drafts.body:
ATTORNEY REVIEW ONLY — DO NOT SEND/POST.
Target: Paul Lee
Public fact hook / hypothesis: Patlytics is the most ironic prospect of the night — they build AI for patents, so they're simultaneously a potential client (needing their own IP strategy) and in the same industry as Whiteford's target practice. Their $40M Series B and expanding autonomous AI agent roadmap suggests they're actively filing their own patents. Rivian is a Patlytics client but also a Patlytics co-founder (RJ Scaringe) connection — interesting overlap. Attorney should evaluate whether Patlytics is a 'beachhead' prospect (they use AI patent tools, so Whiteford's education resonates directly with their product mission) or a competitor adjacency concern.
Suggested lead magnet: AI Patent Strategy Scorecard — /ai-patent-strategy-scorecard
LinkedIn awareness draft exists for internal review only; do not post, tag, or trigger workflows without exact approval.

Internal LinkedIn awareness draft:
There's a funny irony at Patlytics.

They build AI that automates patent drafting. They save attorneys 15 hours per application. They're used by 40% of AmLaw 100 firms.

But here's the thing nobody asks: Who's protecting the IP that makes Patlytics work?

When your core product IS AI-generated patent applications — your own patent portfolio strategy is your product's foundation. And the more advanced you get, the harder that question becomes:

If your platform's AI generates novel claims, who is the inventor? Did the human engineer define the invention? The data scientist train the model? The customer who provided the raw data?

The company that sells patent automation can't skip its own patent strategy.

For #patent-professionals: the tools change. The fundamentals of who contributed what don't.

Educational starting point: AI Patent Strategy Scorecard
https://whiteford-ai-law-pages.vercel.app/ai-patent-strategy-scorecard

Guardrail: no outreach, email/SMS, workflow enrollment, trigger tags, LinkedIn/social action, Clio writes, public/client-facing changes, or live CRM/Supabase sync without Jeff exact approval.
